name: sre

findings.message: The new guard hard-stops the pipeline before pr-delivery is reached, so the `pr.delivery.blocked` event (emitted by pr-delivery when pr-open refuses, plugin.sh:222) is never emitted for `fail`-outcome groups under `on_member_error=continue` (the map-group default at line 3689); consumers monitoring that event to detect 'a review found a problem' lose the signal entirely.

For groups whose members only `fail` (no unfinished outcomes), `_ZB_MAP_UNFINISHED` is empty so the `parallel.group.complete` event fires with `verdict=pass` (line 3715) immediately before the new guard emits `pipeline.end status=failed`, producing a contradictory event stream with no intervening `stage.fail` for the map group; this pre-existing misleading event is now worsened because a hard-stop follows it.

When the guard fires because of a `fail`-outcome member (not an unfinished one), `_ZB_MAP_UNFINISHED` is empty so the error log reads 'a member did not pass' with no indication of which lens failed; the summary file holds the detail but the log entry is generic.

The new guard suppresses `eb_emit_event` errors with `2>/dev/null || true`, inconsistent with the `_rc != 0` failure path at lines 3720–3721 which does not, so an event-bus failure during the new guard's `pipeline.end` emission is silently swallowed rather than surfaced.

The hard-stop returns 1 before any later pipeline stages execute; any template that places cleanup or notification stages after the review map group will have them silently bypassed on review failure — this is the intended fail-fast behavior per the issue, but it removes any opportunity for post-failure teardown in templates that rely on it.

The new guard writes `_zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$state_file" "$_mg_id" "failed"` but the pre-existing `_rc != 0` failure path (lines 3718–3727) for the same map group does not, creating asymmetric state-file contents between the two failure paths and making the state schema depend on which exit triggered the stop.

reason: the sre lens found no high or critical problem the change introduced that fails it
